properties.description:
`crates/reflow2-core/tests/detect.rs` — 7 cases for `release_without_manifest` plus 1 that guards the sibling `release_without_epoch` after it was hardened.

The helper builds healthy cuts — each release pinned to its own epoch, deployed to a shared environment, shipping one artifact — and each test then breaks exactly ONE thing, so a case cannot pass for a reason it does not name.

WHAT IS COVERED: a deployed release stripped of its manifest is reported, and its evidence names how many releases DO carry one; releases with manifests are silent; a release still labelled `planned` while deployed IS reported; a pinned but undeployed release is silent, because the manifest can still land; an unpinned release is left to `release_without_epoch` AND that sibling is asserted to report it, so nothing falls between the two rules; a design where no release records contents at all is silent, one whole-graph fact rather than one alarm per release; and two empty releases get two different gap ids, so an acknowledgement cannot carry from one cut to the next.

⭐ THE CASE THAT EARNED ITS KEEP: `a_status_still_reading_planned_does_not_exempt_a_published_release`. Writing the sibling's `planned` exemption into this rule looked obviously right and would have exempted the only real instance — rel:v0380 was tagged, published, deployed and asset-verified while its status still read `planned`. The test asserts the release really is in that mislabelled shape before asserting the gap fires, so a helper that quietly set the status could not make it pass while testing nothing.

The same case then found the hole in the SIBLING, which had trusted `status` unconditionally since BL-122. `release_without_epoch` now exempts a `planned` release only while it is UNDEPLOYED, with its own test covering both sides of that clause.

MEASURED AGAINST REALITY BEFORE IT WAS WRITTEN: all 40 releases in reflow2's own design were checked for the epoch + deploy + zero-INCLUDES shape. Zero would fire — every release carries a manifest — so the rule adds no false positives to the design that motivated it.
properties.findings:
2026-08-21: `cargo test -p reflow2-core --no-default-features --test detect` — 70 passed, 0 failed. The whole core suite is green at exit 0, clippy and fmt clean.

THE RUN THAT MATTERED WAS THE RED ONE. `an_unpinned_release_is_left_to_its_sibling_detector` failed on first run, asserting that `release_without_epoch` would report the release this rule declines. It did not — because the sibling exempted any release whose status read `planned`, and the helper leaves `Release.status` at its `planned` default. That red test is what exposed the sibling's own status-trust hole, which had been there since BL-122 and would have excused the next cut published while mislabelled. The sibling was then hardened to exempt a planned release only while UNDEPLOYED, and the failing assertion passes for the right reason rather than being relaxed.

MEASURED FIRST, ON REALITY: before the detector was written, all 40 Releases in reflow2's own design were scored for the epoch + deploy + zero-INCLUDES shape. Zero fire. The same sweep is what found that rel:v0380 still carries `status: planned` while tagged, published and deployed — which is the fact the status clause is built around.
properties.name: A deployed release with an empty manifest is reported, and a mislabelled status does not exempt it
